carousels.name: 4 facts that make p*rn addiction a real health issue (ICD-11)

slides.title: 4 facts that make p*rn addiction [[a real health issue.]]
slides.sub: It's not a joke, a phase or a moral failing.

slides.title: WHO [[recognises]] it
slides.body: The World Health Organization's ICD-11 includes compulsive sexual behaviour disorder (since 2019) — covering sexual behaviour people struggle to control, which for many includes p*rn.

slides.title: Facts [[1–2]]
items: It's about control — not how often, but whether you can stop.
It causes real distress — in work, relationships and mental health.

slides.title: Facts [[3–4]]
items: It's treatable — therapy and support help many people quit p*rn.
Only a professional can diagnose it — but you can take it seriously now.

slides.title: What to [[do]]
items: Stop calling it a joke if it's hurting you.
Don't wait for it to get worse.

slides.title: 5 obstacles introverts face [[when they try to give up p*rn.]]
slides.sub: Quiet isn't the problem. Isolation is.

slides.title: Obstacles [[1–2]]
items: Lots of alone time — the setting p*rn needs most.
Recharging at home often means recharging on screens.

slides.title: Obstacles [[3–4]]
items: Hard to ask for help — talking feels like effort.
Big groups feel draining, so you skip them.

slides.title: You [[overthink]]
slides.body: You replay urges, slips and p*rn memories in your head. Thinking about it isn't the same as dealing with it.

slides.title: Introvert-friendly [[fixes]]
items: Recharge offline — books, walks, music, building something.
Text check-ins instead of calls if that's easier.
Write it down instead of replaying it.

slides.title: 4 types of guys at the end of No Nut November [[— and only one stays off p*rn.]]
slides.sub: 2 days left. Be honest about which one you are.

slides.title: The [[binger]]
slides.body: Counts down to Dec 1, then makes up for lost time. 30 days of work, gone in a weekend of p*rn.

slides.title: The [[coaster]]
slides.body: Finishes, relaxes, drops every routine. Slides back to p*rn slowly — and doesn't notice until it's daily again.

slides.title: Types [[3–4]]
items: The restarter: slipped, quit, waits for "a fresh month."
The builder: finishes, sets the next goal, keeps the routines.

items: Set your next goal before Day 30 ends.
If you slipped, restart today — not on the 1st.
